title: Tour Cancelled After You Booked Flights? What to Do Next
excerpt: Tour cancelled after booking flights? A calm six-step plan: refund first, card dispute next, then the flights. Book flights once the departure is confirmed.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

A tour cancelled after booking flights leaves you two problems, not one: get the tour money back and rescue the flights. Work them in order: written cancellation and refund request first, card dispute or insurance claim second, airline change third. Then adopt the rule that prevents the mess: book flights only once the departure is confirmed, or on a flexible fare.

MoneyHelper explains how Section 75 and chargeback work, including their conditions and limits.

Key facts

Fact Detail
Situation The tour is cancelled; the flights still fly. Two separate problems, solved in order
First move Get the cancellation in writing, then request the refund in writing the same day
US card disputes Fair Credit Billing Act billing-error disputes: generally within 60 days of the statement date
UK card protection Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act 1974: a single item costing more than £100 and up to £30,000 bought on a credit card
Chargeback Card-scheme rule, usually claimed within 120 days, sometimes longer for services not yet delivered
EU linked travel arrangements Insolvency protection for money paid to the trader who linked the services; not a general right to a refund
Airline change fees Vary by airline, route and fare class: check the airline's own fee table before paying
When a Sawa date cancels A forming day-tour date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four travellers. If it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged, and another date is suggested
The rule Book flights once the departure confirms (the GoAhead), or keep them flexible

Your Egypt tour was cancelled, but the flights are still confirmed, still paid for, and still leaving on time. Stay calm: this is a paperwork problem, not a lost holiday. A tour cancelled after booking flights splits into two separate jobs: recover the tour payment, then move the flights to dates that work. Each job has a known route and a deadline. This post walks through the steps in order, then explains the booking habit that makes the problem rare. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, was founded by a guide who has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, and charges nothing until a departure is confirmed.

Tour cancelled after booking flights: the six-step plan

Work the two problems in order: secure the tour refund first, then fix the flights. Most steps need only your booking reference and the cancellation notice.

  1. Get the cancellation in writing. Ask the operator for a written notice stating the tour is cancelled and your payment will be refunded. Every later claim (card dispute, insurer, ombudsman) leans on this document.
  2. Request the refund in writing. Reply to the cancellation with a clear refund demand, citing your booking reference and the amount. Card issuers usually expect you to have asked the merchant first.
  3. Check how you paid. Credit card, debit card, bank transfer and insurance each open a different money-back route. The table below compares them.
  4. Hold the airline seat you have. Do not cancel the flight in your first call: a change to new dates usually costs less than a cancel-and-rebook. Ask for the change fee in writing before agreeing to anything.
  5. File the money claims. Start the card chargeback within your card's dispute window; if your policy has a section that responds, lodge an insurance claim with the cancellation notice, booking confirmation and proof of payment attached.
  6. Rebook the tour for the new flight dates. Once the airline confirms the change, pick a departure that is already confirmed to run, or one whose filling deadline sits comfortably after your new arrival.

Which route gets your money back?

Usually the fastest route is the one that matches how you paid: an operator refund if the company is trading, a card dispute if it stalls, insurance only if your policy has the right section. The four main routes compare like this:

Route Works best when Watch out for
Operator refund The company is still trading and replies Slow replies: set a 14-day deadline before escalating
Card chargeback The operator refuses or ignores your refund request Deadlines apply: usually 120 days, and the issuer decides each case
Section 75 claim (UK) A single credit-card purchase of more than £100 and up to £30,000 The card company is jointly liable; claims can take weeks
Travel insurance Your policy has a named supplier-failure section, or the tour cost is covered for a reason you can claim Standard cancellation cover does not usually pay when the company cancels; you pay the excess and need full documents

Recommendation: send the written refund request the same day the cancellation arrives. If nothing lands within 14 days, start the card dispute. Do not wait for the insurer first. Exact deadlines vary by country and card scheme, so ask your card issuer.

How does a card chargeback work?

A card chargeback asks your card issuer to reverse a payment because the service was not delivered, and a cancelled tour is exactly that. Chargeback is a card-scheme rule rather than a law. The usual window is 120 days, counted from the purchase or from the date the service was due, and for services bought well in advance the outer limit can be longer. Write to the issuer, name the merchant, and say the tour was cancelled and never supplied.

In the United States, the Fair Credit Billing Act gives you the right to dispute a billing error on a credit card, generally within 60 days of the statement date. In the United Kingdom, Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act 1974 makes the card company jointly liable for a credit-card purchase costing more than £100 and up to £30,000, so you can claim from the card company itself. A card deposit can bring the whole price within the Act, and you generally have six years to claim.

One more angle for European travellers: EU rules on linked travel arrangements apply when a trader helps you book a second travel service shortly after the first. They give insolvency protection for the money you paid that trader. They do not turn a cancelled tour into a guaranteed refund, and flights you booked separately on your own generally fall outside them.

Will travel insurance pay out?

Often not, and this surprises people. Standard trip-cancellation cover pays when you cancel for a covered reason such as illness. When the tour company cancels, the company owes you the refund. Insurance responds only if your policy has a named end-supplier failure section and the company has gone out of business, and many policies leave that section out. Check your wording before you count on it. If you bought a cancel-for-any-reason upgrade, it refunds only part of the costs.

How do you rescue non-refundable flights?

Ask the airline for a date change before anything else. When a tour is cancelled after booking flights, the flight itself still operates, so no airline refund is due. Your lever is the change fee or a travel credit.

  • Dated example: several large US airlines dropped change fees on standard economy tickets in 2020, but basic economy fares and many international tickets were excluded. Check the fee table for your own fare.
  • If the airline cancels, the rules flip: US Department of Transportation rules require a refund to the original form of payment when an airline cancels a flight, or significantly changes it, and you decline the alternative.
  • Change once, not twice: pick the replacement tour's dates first, then confirm the flight change in a single call.

The Sawa rule: book flights once the departure confirms

Book flights only once the departure confirms: that one rule prevents almost every cancelled-tour-with-live-flights case. On Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), a shared departure is confirmed when four travellers have reserved it: the GoAhead. Reserving a seat on a day tour is free, needs no card, and nothing is charged before it. A forming date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged, and another date is suggested, so there is nothing to refund. For why this happens across the industry, see why Egypt group tours get cancelled.

Once a date confirms, it runs: confirmed dates are not cancelled for low numbers, and a traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded while the tour still goes ahead. On a day tour, a 10% deposit is due as soon as the date confirms, by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. The balance is due 2 days (48 hours) before departure. Cancelling at least 48 hours before departure is a full refund, deposit included; less than 48 hours means the 10% deposit is retained. If a confirmed date has to change because of force majeure, such as riots or a revolution, you get a full refund. Packages and cruises run on longer terms: a 25% deposit at the GoAhead, the balance 14 days before, and a date must reach four by 30 days before departure. The details are on the terms page and the GoAhead promise.

One practical note: because a date can confirm as late as 7 days before the tour, travellers flying in from far away will often want a date that already shows as confirmed, or a flexible or refundable fare while a date is still forming. The departures page shows which dates are forming and which are confirmed. See how it works, read the GoAhead explained, or browse live departures.

Good dates to start with: Giza Uncovered from Cairo, about 4 hours, from €29 per person, or Luxor in Depth, a full day, from €75 per person, as listed in November 2026. Groups are capped at eight, and the departure is operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due.

The verdict on a cancelled tour

A tour cancelled after booking flights is recoverable: a written refund request, then a card dispute for the tour money, and a date change or credit for the flights. Insurance helps only if your policy has the right section. Then make the problem rare: book flights once a departure confirms, or keep them flexible. Browse confirmed GoAhead departures and reserve free; nothing is charged until the date has four travellers.

faq.q: My tour was cancelled but I already booked flights. What now?
faq.a: Secure the tour refund and fix the flights separately. Ask for the cancellation in writing and request the refund in writing; if the operator stalls, start a card chargeback or a Section 75 claim. Then call the airline and ask for a change to your new tour dates. Expect a change fee unless the fare allows free changes.

faq.q: What if the tour company has gone out of business?
faq.a: Claim from your card first. UK credit-card purchases of more than £100 and up to £30,000 fall under Section 75, which makes the card company jointly liable; a chargeback works in most markets while the scheme deadline allows. Travel insurance pays only if your policy has an end-supplier failure section, so check the wording.

faq.q: How long do I have to dispute the charge on my card?
faq.a: In the United States, generally 60 days from the date the statement was sent, under the Fair Credit Billing Act. A chargeback through the card scheme is usually 120 days. UK Section 75 claims carry a longer window, commonly up to six years in England and Wales. Card schemes set their own deadlines, so ask your issuer and start early.

faq.q: Does the airline owe me anything if only the tour was cancelled?
faq.a: No. The flight is unaffected, so airline refund rules do not apply. Those trigger when the airline cancels or significantly changes the flight and you choose not to travel. Your tools are a date change, a travel credit, or rebooking to the new tour dates. Check the fare conditions before paying any fee.

faq.q: What happens if my Sawa departure never fills?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. A Sawa day-tour date needs four travellers to confirm, the GoAhead, and has until 7 days before the tour to get there. If it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged, and another date is suggested. Once a date is confirmed it runs.

faq.q: Should I rebook the same Egypt tour or pick a different date?
faq.a: Pick the date first, then the tour. Look for a departure that already has its GoAhead, or a forming date whose deadline falls well after your new flights land. Keep the same itinerary if it suited you; otherwise Sawa lists day tours from €29 per person, as listed in November 2026.
